terms.definition: The energy change when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions.
terms.examiner: Exothermic as Edexcel defines it. It becomes more exothermic with smaller ions and higher charges.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from an element in its standard state.
terms.examiner: For chlorine it is ½Cl₂(g) → Cl(g).

terms.definition: The energy change when each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms gains an electron to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions.
terms.examiner: The first is usually exothermic; the second is endothermic because an electron is added to an ion that is already negative.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous ions is dissolved in water to form aqueous ions.
terms.examiner: Always exothermic; more exothermic for small, highly charged ions.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid dissolves in water to form a solution in which the ions do not interact.
terms.examiner: Enthalpy change of solution = sum of the hydration enthalpies − lattice energy.

terms.definition: The distortion of the electron cloud of an anion by a neighbouring cation.
terms.examiner: Small, highly charged cations polarise large anions most. An experimental lattice energy more exothermic than the theoretical one shows some covalent character.
